analyst_view.overall: Early view: Leganés are 17th and have not won since Luis Carrión replaced Rubén Albés in October (a draw with Mallorca, then 4-3 and 3-1 defeats), and they concede a lot. Sabadell, back in professional football this season, are 12th with one of the league's tighter defences but score very little away from home. Javi Montero's red-card ban should be served against Burgos on 13 November.

goals.text: The numbers say 1.9 goals. Leganés' defence is leaky (23 conceded), but Sabadell have scored only four goals in seven away games and one preview said they have lost joint top scorer Nicholas Gioacchini to a cruciate ligament injury, so I stay close to the site's low number.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Leganés under Carrión dominate the ball at home (63% and nine corners against Albacete), and Sabadell sit deep away, so most corners should come from the home side, with a total near the site's number.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.2 cards. I lean higher: Leganés took five yellows and a straight red against Albacete, three of their players (Pulido, Kechta and Marvel) have already reached five yellows, and the relegation pressure on Carrión's side is growing.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.4 shots. The total looks fair, although I would expect most of the shots from Leganés (17 against Albacete) rather than Sabadell, whose away attack has been thin.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.7 shots on target. Leganés put seven on target against Albacete, with Álvaro Morata their main threat despite missing a penalty, and Sabadell create little, so I stay with the number.
